name: MathlibAnnex.Matrix.det_smul_vecMul_nonsingInv_eq_updateRowDet
title: Cramer’s rule for coordinates of a row

content.display_title: Cramer’s rule for coordinates of a row
content.one_sentence_role: Expresses a row in the basis of the rows of an invertible square matrix through row-replacement determinants.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $A$ be an $n$-by-$n$ matrix over a field, with $\det A\ne0$, and let $r$ be a row of length $n$. If $A[j\leftarrow r]$ denotes replacement of row $j$ by $r$, then

$$ (\det A)(rA^{-1})_j=\det(A[j\leftarrow r])\qquad(1\le j\le n).$$
content.assumptions: The scalar system is an arbitrary field, $n\ge0$, and $r$ is any row. Nonvanishing of $\det A$ is the exact condition ensuring that the matrix inverse is an inverse.
content.conclusion: The coordinate row $c=rA^{-1}$ satisfies $cA=r$, and each coordinate is $c_j=\det(A[j\leftarrow r])/\det A$. If $n=0$, the equality is between the two empty coordinate families.
content.proof_summary: Apply Cramer’s rule to the transpose, then identify each transposed replacement determinant.

proof_steps.text:
Write $c=rA^{-1}$. Since $\det A\ne0$, the inverse exists and

$$cA=r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A^{\mathsf T}c^{\mathsf T}=r^{\mathsf T}.$$

Apply the column form of Cramer's rule to the system on the right. Its coefficient matrix satisfies $\det(A^{\mathsf T})=\det A\ne0$, so it gives

$$(\det A)c_j=\det\bigl((A^{\mathsf T})[\text{column }j\leftarrow r^{\mathsf T}]\bigr).$$

The replaced-column matrix is exactly the transpose of the replaced-row matrix:

$$\begin{aligned}
(A^{\mathsf T})[\text{column }j\leftarrow r^{\mathsf T}]
   &=(A[j\leftarrow r])^{\mathsf T},\\
(\det A)(rA^{-1})_j
   &=\det((A[j\leftarrow r])^{\mathsf T})\\
   &=\det(A[j\leftarrow r]).
\end{aligned}$$

Dividing by $\det A\ne0$ gives the stated coordinate formula. For $n=0$ there is no coordinate $j$ to check.

content.lean_realization_notes: The row convention is essential: the unknown coordinates multiply $A$ on the left. The source obtains this formula by applying the column form of Cramer’s rule to the transpose; replacing a column of the transpose replaces the corresponding row before transposition.
